clue.text: Poke one's nose into group of servicemen with a candid humour, leading to hospital

indicators.note: the earlier pieces lead on to the last one, which comes at the end

parts.note: a mess is a body of service personnel who eat together
round can mean plain-spoken or outspoken, as in a round rebuke
wit is humour or cleverness with words
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A busybody intrudes on a squad of soldiers, cracks frank jokes, and ends up in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Candid' for ROUND uses an older sense: a round statement is a blunt, outspoken one.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle or interfere with something is the idiomatic sense of poking one's nose into it.

clue.text: What generates interest is Araucaria's home hosting one old Greek king

indicators.note: hosting means holding a guest inside, so the next piece goes within

parts.note: the setter Araucaria speaking of himself, so Araucaria's means my
taken as the word itself
in means at home, as in staying in
a Theban was a citizen of ancient Thebes in Greece
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: The setter boasts that his house has entertained a Greek monarch of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One old Greek king' tempts you to look for a single named king, but it is three pieces; the setter's pseudonym stands for 'my'.
explanation.definitionFit: Savings deposited with a lender earn interest, so deposited cash is what yields it.

clue.text: Ray to be replacing Rhode Island in Dutch Guiana

indicators.note: in puts the new piece inside what is left of the country's name
replacing says a piece of the country's name is removed to make way for another

parts.note: Surinam, the former Dutch colony in South America, was once called Dutch Guiana
RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island
be is the verb to be itself

explanation.surface: Someone called Ray is to take the place of a Rhode Islander posted to Dutch Guiana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replacing' is loose here: the new piece does not sit in the gap the state's letters leave, but one place further on.
explanation.definitionFit: A single shaft of light from the sun is a ray of sunshine.

clue.text: Awfully cute little quadruplets that hold 6

definitions.note: 6 is the answer to 6 down, whose first word is water, so these are things that hold water

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are put together badly, so they are rearranged

parts.note: quads is the short, informal word for quadruplets

explanation.surface: Four tiny babies are terribly sweet, and they somehow hold water.
explanation.walkthrough: The 6 refers to 6 down, WATER UNDER THE BRIDGE, of which only WATER is needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqueducts are bridges or channels built to carry water across country.

clue.text: 6 animal loses tail and so on turning up inside with a group

indicators.note: inside says one piece sits within the other
loses tail means the last letter of the animal is dropped

parts.note: 6 down begins with water, and a water animal is an otter

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up reads the piece from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: etc, short for et cetera, means and so on

explanation.surface: A river creature loses its tail and keeps on flipping over among its companions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loses tail' leaves OTTE; 'turning up' gives CTE, which goes inside after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet or octette is a set of eight performers or things, so it is one kind of group.

clue.text: Get a taste of ink in the club?

definitions.text: Get a taste of ink in the club?

parts.words: Get a taste of ink in the club?
parts.note: to taste ink you would lick a pen's nib, and the two words together name an old golf club

explanation.surface: Someone at their club sucks a pen and tastes the ink.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is a pen-point plus a lick; read as one, it is a club used in golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A niblick is an old name for an iron golf club with a steeply angled face, roughly a nine iron.

clue.text: Deterrent rebid, Waugh's work for passing time?

definitions.note: events that have gone by and no longer matter, like a river that has already flowed past

indicators.note: work here means to rework or knead, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: the novelist Evelyn Waugh's surname, with the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: A bridge player's discouraging second bid is treated as a piece of fiction by Evelyn Waugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waugh's work' looks like a novel's title; 'work' is the signal to rearrange DETERRENT, REBID and WAUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes past events now beyond changing, as time flows on like a river.

clue.text: Vehicle submerged in a sea of lost umbrellas

indicators.note: submerged in says the answer lies concealed within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A cart sinks into a heap of umbrellas left behind by careless owners.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbrel is a cart, famously the kind that carried prisoners to the guillotine in revolutionary France.

clue.text: See 21
Action that doesn't take place in Union St

indicators.note: in, as in being in a state of disorder, lightly signals that the street name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A planned protest or event fails to happen on Union Street.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is only the faint 'in'; 'Union St' is the fodder, its abbreviation letters included.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonsuit is a legal ruling ending a lawsuit because the plaintiff has no case, so the case never proceeds.

clue.text: Robin's mate's second in one increase?

definitions.note: read as one in crease, someone standing at the crease in cricket

indicators.note: in puts the short piece inside the superhero's name

parts.note: the comic-book hero Batman is the partner of Robin, the Boy Wonder

explanation.surface: Batman's sidekick gets a second boost of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'increase' into 'in crease': the crease is the line in cricket where the player facing the bowler stands.
explanation.definitionFit: The player taking guard at the crease in cricket is the one with the bat, so 'one in crease' describes him.

clue.text: Give up the harvest

definitions.meaning: the crop a field produces, its output

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to surrender, and the noun is the amount of crop or return produced.

clue.text: Transporter (not car) in chart designed by ship's captain

indicators.note: in places the trimmed transporter inside the rearranged chart
designed suggests the letters of chart are laid out afresh, rearranged
not says the following word is taken away from the transporter

parts.note: a carrier is anything that transports goods or people
taken as written

explanation.surface: A naval commander plots a vehicle, minus its car, on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transporter' is not taken as written; it needs a synonym that begins with the car to be removed.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Athens a trierarch commanded a trireme, the oared warship, so he was its captain.

clue.text: Mention of a mechanical piece in the isthmus

indicators.note: in puts the extracted piece inside the narrow strip of land

parts.note: an isthmus is a neck of land joining two larger areas

indicators.note: piece means only part of the words a mechanical is used, the tail being cut away

explanation.surface: Someone refers to a machine part found on a narrow strip of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' looks like a noun for a machine part, but it signals that only the front of 'a mechanical' is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A namecheck is a public mention of someone by name, such as a thank-you in a speech.

clue.text: Norman ruler starts to be added to the jackpot

indicators.note: starts means only the opening part of the lottery word is used, dropping its ending

parts.words: to be added to the jackpot
parts.note: a lottery rollover is unwon prize money carried forward and added to the next jackpot

explanation.surface: A Norman leader begins by putting money into the prize pot.
explanation.walkthrough: ROLLOVER is the British lottery term for an unwon jackpot carried into the next draw; its start, ROLLO, is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rollo was the Viking chief who became the first ruler of Normandy in the tenth century.

clue.text: Cycle of duty with pistol has backing (of body?)

definitions.note: something of the body that controls a process, such as a gland or the heart's pacemaker

indicators.note: backing turns the joined pieces round so they read in reverse

parts.note: a rota is a rotating list of duties
the Luger is a German semi-automatic pistol

explanation.surface: A soldier's duty roster plus a gun is supported by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has backing' looks like support for the soldier; it reverses ROTA followed by LUGER as a single run.
explanation.definitionFit: Glands and other organs that control bodily processes are regulators of the body, keeping it in balance.

clue.text: Complaint as of the "murmuring of innumerable bees"?

definitions.meaning: an ailment, here an itchy skin rash, urticaria

definitions.text: as of the "murmuring of innumerable bees"?
definitions.meaning: where bees live and murmur in huge numbers, quoting Tennyson's line about bees

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation comes from Tennyson's poem The Princess: 'the murmuring of innumerable bees'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an itchy skin rash and the boxes where colonies of honeybees are kept.

clue.text: Meat in the oven is only half cooked

indicators.note: in says the answer is found within the following words, here the run oven is only

explanation.surface: A cook warns that the joint in the oven is still only partly done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half cooked' is surface colour; the answer runs through 'oVEN IS ONly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Venison is the flesh of deer eaten as food.

clue.text: Reduce status of dog warden?

indicators.note: of, as in made of, lightly says the answer is formed from the letters of dog warden

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to demote the official who catches stray dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is signalled only by 'of' and the question mark: DOG WARDEN has the same letters as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To downgrade someone is to demote them, lowering their rank or standing.

clue.text: Medicine man should be here as rainmaker?

definitions.text: Medicine man should be here as rainmaker?

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, a medical man
ought means should, as in you ought to go

explanation.surface: A tribal shaman ought to be summoned to bring on the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a rainmaking medicine man is needed where the land is parched.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spell with no rainfall is exactly when a rainmaker would be called in.

clue.text: Fight with the French after peace

indicators.note: after says the French article follows the other pieces

parts.note: rest means peace or quiet
le is the masculine form of the in French

explanation.surface: A battle against the French breaks out once peace is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrestle is to grapple or struggle with an opponent, a form of fighting.

clue.text: Embarrassed by prize that contains little power

indicators.note: that contains says the prize holds another piece inside it

parts.note: an award is a prize
kW, the kilowatt, is a unit of power, shortened

explanation.surface: Someone is red-faced over a prize that brings very little influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little power' is the abbreviation for a unit of power, the kilowatt.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward can mean uncomfortable or self-conscious, the feeling of being embarrassed.

clue.text: Indian city's veto on quantity

indicators.note: on says the first piece sits on top of the second, in front of it in an across answer

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition, a veto
galore means in abundance, in great quantity

explanation.surface: An Indian city puts a ban on bulk amounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Galore' is usually an adverb, 'in plenty', standing here for a great quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangalore, now officially Bengaluru, is a major city in southern India.

clue.text: Freefone between Alison and Theodore, a new arrangement in the first home to which the marines marched

indicators.note: between places the rearranged phone letters between the two short names

parts.note: Ali is a short form of the name Alison
Theo is a short form of the name Theodore
read as fone set free, its four letters loosed and rearranged

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the early dwelling

parts.note: a cave was the first home of early humans

indicators.note: arrangement says the letters of a new are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A free phone call between two people is set up in some new way at a place the marines once marched to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freefone' is read as 'free fone', the second half set free and rearranged; Ali and Theo are pet forms of the two names, and 'arrangement' scrambles A NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: The song A Life on the Ocean Wave is the regimental march of Britain's Royal Marines.

clue.text: Compare plant with symbiotic fungus, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a lichen is a partnership of a fungus with an alga, loosely called a plant

explanation.surface: Someone compares a plant that lives in partnership with a fungus.
explanation.walkthrough: LICHEN can be pronounced 'liken', which is the sense used here.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken one thing to another is to compare them, pointing out a likeness.

clue.text: Sort of box for little gentlemen in trouble

indicators.note: trouble means to stir up or disturb, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: gents is a short, informal form of gentlemen
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some kind of crate is meant for small men who have got into difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: GENTS and IN together are rearranged by 'trouble'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nesting box is a box put up for birds to build their nests in.

clue.text: An island at back of Russian girl

indicators.note: back says the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
an ait is a small island in a river, especially the Thames
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Russian girl is described as an island at the far end.
explanation.walkthrough: AN AIT AT, written in reverse, gives the name; an ait (or eyot) is a small river island, a British word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatiana is a common Russian girl's name, as with the heroine of Pushkin's Eugene Onegin.

clue.text: See 6
